_captured.protocol: MSP v1 for state, MSP v2 for settings

analog.note: pack voltage and current, in the board's units

api_version.note: what protocol version the board speaks

attitude.note: roll, pitch, yaw in tenths of a degree

eeprom_write.note: put the running configuration into flash -- a separate command, never a side effect of a write

eeprom_write_refused.note: the same command on an armed board, which both firmwares refuse in their own code -- and the refusal is a frame, not silence

fc_variant.note: BTFL or INAV -- the string that decides which name list applies

motor.note: four outputs, in the board's units

rc.note: the channel values the board is flying on

setting_absent.note: a name the board does not have -- a refusal, not an empty answer

setting_info_known.note: the same name's description: pgn, type, min, max, default

setting_known.note: ask a setting by name; the board answers 'name = value'

setting_read_after_write.note: the same setting read back after that write -- the board really does hold 1200 now, so a read-back can agree or disagree with a captured fact rather than with the app's own optimism

setting_write.note: a write, answered with what the board holds -- or in INAV's case, with nothing at all, which is why the read-back exists

setting_write_refused.note: the same write with a value outside the board's own range -- the board refuses rather than clamping to a number nobody asked for

status.note: arming flags, sensor health, the current mode box, and the profile

status_armed.note: the arming flags with the armed bit set -- the gate reads this and nothing else
